Article Title: 'Rubbing salt into wounds': BJP targets Rahul over Nov 1 rally, recalls 1984 anti-Sikh riots
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Bharatiya Janata Party on Saturday upped the ante against Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi, accusing him of rubbing salt into the wounds of the Sikh community by holding an INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan on November 1 - the anniversary of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots in Delhi following the assassination of former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.Addressing a press conference, senior BJP leader Ravi Shankar Prasad questioned the Congress leader's insistence on holding the rally on the date."Why is Rahul Gandhi so adamant about holding his rally in Delhi on November 1? This issue is being raised very seriously by our party. November 1 is a day that holds deep emotional significance for the Sikh community, as they remember the 1984 massacre with profound sorrow," Prasad said."So, by creating a storm at Ramlila Maidan on November 1, what kind of salt does Rahul Gandhi want to rub into their wounds?" he asked.The BJP leader also said that many members of the opposition alliance were not satisfied with the decision to hold the rally on November 1."We have heard that many members of their alliance were also not satisfied with this decision. We have also received information that a virtual meeting was convened on October 22 to discuss this issue.However, since many allies did not attend, the meeting was postponed," he said."We have also learnt that several allies were unhappy with the November 1 date and had suggested that the rally be postponed to a later date. This reflects Rahul Gandhi's true face. When he insists on something, he refuses to listen to anyone. If he is determined to have his way, he will go ahead, even if it means cruelly mocking the sentiments of the Sikh community," the BJP leader said.The opposition rally aims to ramp up pressure on the government over the "vote chori" issue and demand Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.On October 12, protests over the "vote theft" charge reached the Supreme Court's doorstep, with opposition leaders, activists and civil society members participating in a 'March for Democracy' along a heavily barricaded route in Delhi and filing a joint petition against the SIR.Rahul hosted INDIA bloc leaders for tea at his home on October 13. After the meeting, the opposition bloc vowed to continue resisting and take the "vote chori" fight to its logical conclusion.
Article Summary: Bharatiya Janata Party accuses Rahul Gandhi of rubbing salt into the wounds of the Sikh community by holding an INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan on November 1. November 1 is the anniversary of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots in Delhi following the assassination of former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.

Article Title: Bihar MLC polls: 5.32 lakh voters to decide fate of 150 candidates across 8 seats, JD(U) rift adds intrigue
Article Text:
Polling began at 8 am today for eight seats in the Bihar Legislative Council (Representative image)





PATNA: Polling for biennial elections to eight Bihar Legislative Council seats began at 8 am on Friday amid tight security, with 5.32 lakh voters eligible to decide the fate of 150 candidates, officials said.Voting will continue till 4 pm for four Graduates and four Teachers constituencies, they said.The combined electorate stands at 5,32,847, including 1,46,611 women and 37 third-gender voters, across 933 polling stations. Counting of votes will take place on October 27.The contest in the Patna Graduates constituency has drawn attention following an open rift within the JD(U), with Mokama MLA Anant Singh backing Jan Suraaj Party candidate Anuj Singh against his own party's nominee, Neeraj Kumar.Kumar, a former minister and a close aide of former chief minister Nitish Kumar, is seeking a fourth consecutive term from the seat.Anant Singh has extended support to Anuj Singh, alleging that Neeraj Kumar had worked against him during last year's assembly elections.Apart from Patna Graduates, the other constituencies going to polls are Darbhanga Graduates, Tirhut Graduates, Kosi Graduates, Patna Teachers, Darbhanga Teachers, Tirhut Teachers and Saran Teachers.The terms of the sitting MLCs are due to expire on November 16.The BJP has fielded candidates in four constituencies, including three sitting MLCs seeking re-election, while the JD(U) has nominated candidates for the remaining four seats.The BJP nominees are MLCs Nawal Kishor Yadav, NK Yadav and Sarvesh Kumar, who are seeking re-election from Patna Teachers, Kosi Graduates and Tirhut Graduates, respectively.The party has also fielded Narendra Kumar Singh from Tirhut Teachers, a seat currently held by Sanjay Kumar Singh of the CPI, a constituent of the opposition INDIA bloc.The Jan Suraaj Party (JSP), led by Prashant Kishor, is contesting all eight seats. The party revised its candidate list after its initial announcement, replacing Bhushan Jha with Shyam Nandan Yadav in Tirhut Teachers and Ravindra Yadav with Mohammad Imtiyaz (Noorani) in Darbhanga Graduates.(With PTI inputs)
Article Summary: Voting will continue till 4 pm for four Graduates and four Teachers constituencies. The combined electorate stands at 5,32,847, including 1,46,611 women and 37 third-gender voters. Counting of votes will take place on October 27.

NEW DELHI: Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann has alleged that he was kept waiting for around two hours at Delhi airport after returning from Paris, claiming that officials repeatedly cited luggage checks as the reason for the delay. Mann also alleged that the head of ustoms at the airport, identified as Manish, is the brother of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.“They kept us seated there for two hours, repeatedly saying that they were checking our luggage. But they found nothing in our luggage. The head of customs at Delhi Airport, Manish, is the real brother of Gyanesh Kumar,” Mann said.The allegation comes after the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) claimed that Mann was detained for three hours at the airport late on Monday and issued a challan of Rs 50,000 upon his return from a food trade fair in Paris.AAP state media in-charge Baltej Pannu alleged that the incident was part of a deliberate attempt by the BJP-led Centre to humiliate Mann and undermine Punjab's dignity. He claimed that officials initially told the chief minister that his luggage was still arriving or being checked.According to Pannu, Mann was allowed to leave after several hours but was issued the challan when he was about to depart in his vehicle.Pannu alleged that officials told Mann they were under “tremendous pressure from above”. After the Centre denied him political clearance, the Punjab government approached the Punjab and Haryana high court, which set aside the decision, observing that the Centre “had not explained what that political angle/viewpoint is”.

NEW DELHI: Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) chief Raj Thackeray on Friday accused the BJP of "murdering" democracy by allegedly exerting pressure on the media and using religious polarisation to divert public attention. The barb came after an audio clip triggered a political row over claims of a Rs 500 crore payment to Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange.In a post on X, Thackeray said the 29-minute recording, which has gone viral in Maharashtra, allegedly featured BJP office-bearers, a senior Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) functionary and social media influencers discussing political strategies, media pressure and ways to divert attention from sensitive issues by fuelling religious polarisation.“The chief minister has tried to buy time by saying he’s called for a forensic report on the audio clip, making a show of justice,” Thackeray said, referring to Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis 's announcement of a forensic examination.“But if you actually listen to the conversation in this, you’ll realize it’s nothing short of a murder and rape of democracy itself!” he added.Thackeray said the alleged Rs 500 crore payment mentioned in the recording required an explanation but argued that the broader allegations about attempts to influence the media and public discourse also deserved scrutiny. He urged Fadnavis to investigate the conversations allegedly captured in the clip, rather than limiting the inquiry to verifying the recording's authenticity.The controversy erupted after Jarange released a portion of the recording on Thursday, alleging a conspiracy to silence him and weaken his agitation for Maratha reservation. In one segment, a woman allegedly claims that Rs 500 crore had been delivered to Jarange through Shiv Sena MP Shrikant Shinde, son of deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde.The recording also purportedly contains discussions about Jarange's growing political influence ahead of the 2024 Maharashtra assembly elections and strategies to counter his agitation in the Marathwada region.Fadnavis has said the audio clips and conversations would undergo a thorough forensic examination. Shiv Sena leaders have also sought an investigation, while BJP leaders have questioned the recording's authenticity and the timing of its release. BJP IT minister Ashish Shelar called for an inquiry into how the clip was leaked and reached Jarange, while party spokesperson Navnath Ban suggested it could be AI-generated.
Article Summary: MNS chief Raj Thackeray accused the BJP of "murdering" democracy. The barb came after an audio clip triggered a political row over claims of a Rs 500 crore payment to Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange. He urged Fadnavis to investigate the conversations allegedly captured in the clip.

Controversial hoardings targeting Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav surfaced at a busy crossing in Lucknow on Friday, featuring images of slain gangster-politicians Atiq Ahmed and Mukhtar Ansari alongside jailed senior party leader Mohammad Azam Khan , ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections.According to ANI, the hoardings appeared at the National PG College crossing and carried a rhyming Hindi slogan aimed at the SP.The poster read, “Sapaiyon ka kya bharosa — Chai, samosa, rasmalai, saare mafia apne bhai”, alleging links between the party and criminal figures. He also alleged that the government had deliberately damaged Mohammad Ali Jauhar University in Rampur.“I have just met with Azam Khan, and he will receive justice. I inquired about his well-being, and we discussed how the university has been ruined,” Yadav said.He further alleged that Khan's family had faced an exceptional degree of political persecution.“As for the injustice inflicted, perhaps in all of political history, no other family has faced as many false cases as the family of Azam Khan,” he said.

Article Title: Watch: Andhra Pradesh ex-minister Vidadala Rajini pushed to ground by cop near her residence in Chilakaluripet

What happened ?





PALNADU: A video purportedly showing former Andhra Pradesh minister Vidadala Rajini being pushed to the ground by a police sub-inspector near her residence in Chilakaluripet has surfaced. The incident reportedly occurred after Rajini questioned the police for stopping YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) leader and Yadlapadu ZPTC candidate Pandula Bullabbayi from entering her residence.The incident reportedly occurred amid allegations by the YSRCP that its candidates were being threatened and pressured to withdraw their nominations during the local body election process.According to the details provided, Bullabbayi was stopped by police from entering Rajini’s residence. Rajini questioned the police over the move, following which the confrontation reportedly took place. The Chilakaluripet Rural sub-inspector allegedly pushed the former minister to the ground.In an earlier post on X, Rajini had accused those in power of undermining democracy in Chilakaluripet. Democracy is permanent!” Rajini wrote in the post.(With agency inputs)

Article Title: Ex-Congress minister's wife elected sarpanch unopposed for 7th time in Rajasthan village
Article Text:
Bhikhidevi, wife of former Congress minister Hemaram Choudhary, was elected sarpanch without opposition





JAISALMER: Bhikhidevi, wife of former Congress minister Hemaram Choudhary, was elected unopposed Friday as sarpanch of Virendra Nagar gram panchayat in Baytoo panchayat samiti for a seventh consecutive term, ahead of the first phase of Panchayati Raj elections in Barmer district.Bhikhidevi has held the post for 35 years. No rival candidate remained in the fray after the completion of the nomination and withdrawal process, paving the way for her unopposed election.Thanking the villagers for their continued support, Bhikhidevi said she would strive to live up to their trust and continue working for the village’s development and welfare.In another unopposed election, Dhan Singh Mausari was elected sarpanch of Mausari gram panchayat under Gadra Road panchayat samiti. He was the only candidate to file a nomination for the post. All seven ward panch members in the gram panchayat were also elected unopposed.Polling for sarpanch and ward panch posts in the remaining gram panchayats of the district will be held Saturday from 7 am to 6 pm. Counting will begin after polling concludes, with results expected by night.The election for deputy sarpanch will be held Sunday.
Article Summary: Bhikhidevi has held the post for 35 years. No rival candidate remained in the fray after the completion of the nomination and withdrawal process, paving the way for her unopposed election. Polling for sarpanch and ward panchayats of the district will be held Saturday from 7 am to 6 pm, with results expected by night.

Article Title: ‘Do you eat beef’: Coimbatore teacher under scanner after Dalit Class XI student dies by suicide
Article Text:
Peelamedu police have registered a case involving a teacher, headmaster, and two students related to a student’s suicide





COIMBATORE: Peelamedu police in the city have registered a case under three sections against four people, including two students of a government-aided school, in connection with the suicide of a Scheduled Caste student near Peelamedu.A. Akilan, 16, was a Class XI student of a government-aided school (KK Naidu) near Peelamedu. On Wednesday, his parents went to work while Akilan stayed at their home near Peelamedu.Upon returning from work, his mother, Kowsalya, found him hanging from the ceiling in a bedroom.She lodged a complaint with the Peelamedu police on Wednesday stating that Akilan had informed her that other students in the school were not talking to him after learning that he belonged to a Scheduled Caste.Furthermore, she alleged that the teacher had questioned the student about whether he ate beef, and the headmaster was accused of failing to take action regarding the incident.Peelamedu police have registered a case against the teacher, headmaster, and two fellow students in connection with Akilan's suicide, and further investigation is underway.
Article Summary: A. Akilan, 16, was a Class XI student of a government-aided school near Peelamedu. His mother, Kowsalya, found him hanging from the ceiling in a bedroom. Police have registered a case against the teacher, headmaster, and two fellow students.

Article Title: ‘Cricket personality’, fake investment promises, Rs 24 lakh fraud: How Delhi man duped woman constable
Article Text:
Vikrant Kumar, 26, was taken into custody after reportedly scamming a Delhi Police constable of Rs 24 lakh

Accused used Instagram, WhatsApp to gain constable’s trust

Delhi Police register case under BNS





NEW DELHI: A 26-year-old Vicky Tomar has been arrested for allegedly cheating a Delhi Police woman constable of around Rs 24 lakh after approaching her on Instagram under the pretext of seeking guidance on police recruitment through the sports quota, Delhi Police said.The accused, identified as Vikrant Kumar alias Vicky Tomar, allegedly moved the conversation to WhatsApp, where he built familiarity with the constable and portrayed himself as a prominent personality in cricket.He subsequently lured her with promises of high returns on investments, leading to the alleged fraud.According to Delhi Police, the case was registered at Cyber Police Station in Central District on the complaint of the constable.She told police that the accused had initially contacted her on Instagram, claiming he wanted guidance on recruitment to Delhi Police under the sports quota.The interaction later shifted to WhatsApp, where the accused allegedly established a rapport with her and presented himself as a prominent figure in cricket. Police said he then persuaded her to invest money by making false promises of high returns.The constable was allegedly cheated of approximately Rs 24 lakh.An FIR was registered on September 8, 2026, under Sections 318(4), 316(2) and 74 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), police said.Vikrant Kumar has been arrested in connection with the case. Police are now working to identify other potential victims who may have been targeted by the accused.Delhi Police said a detailed press release would be issued after further investigation.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Vikrant Kumar, 26, arrested for allegedly cheating a Delhi Police woman constable of around Rs 24 lakh. Accused approached her on Instagram under the pretext of seeking guidance on police recruitment through the sports quota. He allegedly moved the conversation to WhatsApp, where he built familiarity with the constable and portrayed himself as a prominent personality in cricket.

Article Title: Bombay High Court rules south Mumbai bizman’s extortion case arrest illegal, orders Rs 5 lakh compensation
Article Text:
Bombay High Court

Mumbai:





Bombay High Court on Thursday declared the 2017 arrest of Malabar Hill businessman Bipin Agrwal illegal, holding that a police sub-inspector acted in collusion with a developer to falsely implicate him in an extortion case Directing the state govt to pay Agrwal Rs 5 lakh as compensation within two weeks, HC also ordered strict action — even suspension, if warranted — against officers involved, including inspector Mahesh Lamkhade of Azad Maidan police station.It also directed HC registry to place the judgment before its administrative committee for appropriate action against the 64th metropolitan magistrate who authorised and continued Agrwal’s custody without recording reasons.Police have attempted to characterise the petitioner as a gangster, history-sheeter or an extortionist without any iota of evidence, said a bench of Justices Kamal Khata and A S Gadkari, while hearing Agarwal’s writ petition.HC observed that police failed to establish why the cash was paid or investigate whether it represented an advance towards a contractual transaction. The court found serious discrepancies in police records, including overwriting in the arrest form, contradictory station diary entries, missing details about the grounds of arrest and alleged suppression of a forensic report.It held that the arrest and subsequent remand were arbitrary, high-handed and carried out without proper application of mind or compliance with statutory safeguards.HC also noted that the offence under Indian Penal Code Section 384 for extortion carried a maximum punishment of three years, yet police failed to demonstrate why his arrest was necessary. The bench found that the notice under Section 41A of the Code of Criminal Procedure was served after the arrest, without giving Agrwal a genuine opportunity to comply.The court held that the magistrate had failed to independently apply judicial mind while authorising continued remand. It acknowledged that the unlawful arrest caused substantial financial loss and irreparable damage to Agrwal’s reputation. The court also disposed of a connected criminal application filed by Seth and Sonal Developers, as it no longer survived following the disposal of the petition.
Article Summary: Bombay High Court declares the 2017 arrest of Malabar Hill businessman Bipin Agrwal illegal. The court found serious discrepancies in police records, including overwriting in the arrest form, contradictory station diary entries, missing details about the grounds of arrest and alleged suppression of a forensic report.

Article Title: Aurangabad division graduates’ constituency: Concerns raised over oversized ballot papers
Article Text:
Voter apathy marks graduates’ constituency polls; oversized ballot papers raise concerns

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





Voter apathy marked the Aurangabad division graduates’ constituency election on Friday, with turnout varying across Marathwada’s eight districts.Out of the 3,26,720 eligible voters across the eight Marathwada districts, 1,91,689 cast their votes, recording a turnout of 58.7%. Dharashiv recorded the highest turnout at 62.5%, with 18,225 of 29,145 voters participating.It was followed by Parbhani at 61.8%, where 16,482 of 26,684 voters cast their ballots, and Hingoli at 61.6%, with 6,352 of 10,315 voters turning out.Jalna and Nanded both recorded a turnout of 59.8%. In Jalna, 19,853 of 33,196 voters exercised their franchise, while in Nanded, 21,942 of 36,687 voters participated. Beed recorded 59.7%, with 34,416 of 57,672 voters casting their votes.Latur recorded a turnout of 56.5%, with 22,412 of 39,703 voters participating. Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, which had the highest number of registered voters at 93,318, recorded the lowest turnout at 55.7%, with 52,007 voters casting their ballots.The unusually large ballot papers, necessitated by the presence of 41 candidates, also raised concerns about the voting process. Maha Vikas Aghadi candidate Pratapsinh Patil questioned the rationale behind their size, alleging that the ballots were getting damaged while being inserted into boxes, which could lead to votes being disqualified.Voters at some polling stations struggled to unfold oversized ballot papers and mark candidates in order of preference, with staff helping them fold the papers. The process proved cumbersome even for graduates.Former MLC Satish Chavan, who has won the constituency three consecutive times, voted at Regional Agricultural Extension Management Institute in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar. Patil, whose name gained prominence during the final phase of campaigning, cast his vote in Dharashiv.MVA candidate Patil demanded that none of the votes should be disqualified simply because the ballot paper got damaged. His views were seconded by BJP MLA Sudhir Mungantiwar.Despite visits by candidates and political leaders, including BJP district president Kishor Shitole, polling remained sluggish at several centres. Some candidates arranged four-wheelers to ferry voters in urban areas and auto rickshaws for those living within five kilometres of polling stations in taluka and semi-urban areas.
Article Summary: Out of the 3,26,720 eligible voters across the eight Marathwada districts, 1,91,689 cast their votes, recording a turnout of 58.7%. Dharashiv recorded the highest turnout at 62.5%, with 18,225 of 29,145 voters participating. Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar recorded the lowest turnout at 55.7%, with 52,007 voters casting their ballots.

Article Title: 2 booked for transferring Rs14.9 lakh from civil hospital account
Article Text:
File photo

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





An assistant superintendent of the district civil hospital at Chikalthana in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar and another person have been booked for allegedly transferring Rs 14.9 lakh from the hospital’s bank account using a cheque bearing a forged signature.The accused have been identified as Deepak Pundlikrao Jadhav, assistant superintendent at the hospital, and Vijay Ramesh Ujed. “The Cidco MIDC police registered the case following a complaint by Gururaj Govind Joshi, the hospital’s administrative officer and drawing and disbursing officer,” deputy commissioner of police (Zone II) Ratnakar Navale said.According to the complaint, a cheque issued against the hospital’s bank account was allegedly signed fraudulently on Oct 19, 2026, around 1.30 pm. The cheque was later issued in Ujed’s name, following which Rs 14,91,272 was credited to his bank account.The alleged irregularity came to light after the administrative officer raised a question over the unjustified transaction. The issue was brought to the notice of the higher-ups before reporting it to the police. The incident has raised concerns over the unauthorised transfer of govt hospital funds through the use of a cheque kept in the custody of an official.Police registered a case on Thursday night and began investigating how a cheque was prepared and processed to transfer money from a hospital’s account.Investigators are examining banking records, cheque-related documents and the transaction trail to determine how the money was transferred. The probe will establish the respective roles of the two accused, whether they acted together to facilitate the transfer and whether anyone else was involved in the alleged offence.“We are yet to establish the full circumstances surrounding the transaction. The allegations against the accused will be subject to investigation,” Navale said, adding that the possibility of involvement of other people cannot be ruled out.
Article Summary: The alleged irregularity came to light after the administrative officer raised a question over the unjustified transaction. The issue was brought to the notice of the higher-ups before reporting it to the police. The incident has raised concerns over the unauthorised transfer of govt hospital funds through the use of a cheque kept in the custody of an official.

Article Title: Manoj Jarange drops audio clip alleging plot to weaken Maratha quota stir, sparks political storm and demand for probe
Article Text:
Manoj Jarange released an audio clip claiming he was offered Rs 500 crore to stop his protest.

(With inputs from PTI)





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange on Thursday released about 10 minutes of a 32-minute audio clip alleging a Rs 500-crore payment to him to call off his agitation, claiming it was part of a conspiracy to weaken the reservation movement. The clip sparked a political controversy, with both opposition and Mahayuti members demanding a thorough probe.After raising the issue at his Dasara rally in Beed, Jarange played the part of the audio clip at a news conference in Ambad tehsil in Jalna on Thursday and demanded a probe. In the clip, a woman allegedly claimed that Rs 500 crore had reached Jarange. The discussion then shifted to Jarange’s rising political clout, efforts to blunt his agitation and plans to rally Maratha leaders against him.Jarange described the recording as an evidence of a conspiracy to weaken the Maratha reservation movement and alleged sustained attempts over the past three years to discredit him. He urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi , chief minister Devendra Fadnavis and deputy CM Eknath Shinde to order an investigation. He also threatened further disclosures if the alleged conspiracy continued.Shiv Sena members demanded a forensic examination of the audio clip. Industries minister Uday Samant said voice samples must be sent to a forensic laboratory to verify their authenticity.He also called for an investigation into who recorded and circulated the clip, and with what intent.Former minister Ramdas Kadam questioned why Jarange had withheld the recording for two years, claiming it dated back to Oct 14, 2024. Sena MP Naresh Mhaske urged Jarange to submit the clip to police and the cyber cell, saying the identities of those heard in the clip must be verified.Terming the audio clip put out by Jarange absolutely fake, IT minister Ashish Shelar also sought an inquiry into the clip’s origins and authenticity. “How it was leaked....how did it reach Jarange and why has he brought it out now... There should be a thorough inquiry,” he said. BJP spokesperson Navnath Ban suggested it could be AI-generated.State minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule said Jarange should file a complaint over his allegation about payment of Rs 500 crore, assuring a “thorough and impartial” probe if evidence was submitted. Talking to reporters over the issue in Jalna, Bawankule said, “If Jarange has concrete evidence regarding the alleged Rs 500 crore payment (as mentioned in the) audio clip and the conspiracy to implicate him, he should register an official complaint with the police or the district collector instead of speaking only to the media. ”Meanwhile, Maharashtra Congress chief Harshwardhan Sapkal demanded an Enforcement Directorate investigation into the alleged money trail.On Wednesday, deputy CM Shinde, speaking with reporters in New Delhi, had dared Jarange to prove his allegation regarding payment of Rs 500 crore. Talking to reporters, Shinde had said no one had been paid (or had received) Rs 500 crore. “He (Jarange) should have verified facts before speaking. He should furnish proof to the agencies concerned and this matter should be probed,” Shinde said.
Article Summary: Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange released about 10 minutes of a 32-minute audio clip alleging a Rs 500-crore payment to him to call off his agitation. Jarange claimed it was part of a conspiracy to weaken the reservation movement. The clip sparked a political controversy, with both opposition and Mahayuti members demanding a thorough probe.

Article Title: Tough fight between two factions of NCP on cards as stage set for MLC polls
Article Text:
Election machinery was in action mode on the eve of MLC poll on Thursday

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar





: The stage is set for polling in the Aurangabad division graduates’ constituency on Friday, where 3,26,701 graduate voters will decide the fate of 41 candidates across 842 polling centres in eight districts. Polling will be held from 8 am to 4 pm, with the counting scheduled for Oct 27.While political equations have turned messy across both Mahayuti and Maha Vikas Aghadi (MVA) camps, the two factions of Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) are largely battling this election as a fight for legacy. The contest is expected to be a direct fight between sitting MLC Satish Chavan of NCP and Pratapsinh Patil of NCP (SP).Within Mahayuti alliance, Sillod Shiv Sena MLA Abdul Sattar campaigned against Chavan, with a few prominent party leaders allegedly siding with Sattar secretly. MVA also faced an internal split after its alliance partner, Shiv Sena (UBT), fielded Dilip Ghuge.Graduate voters will cast their ballots through a preferential voting system, which differs from general elections. Voters must use only the violet sketch pen supplied by the polling officer. Using any other pen, ballpoint, or pencil will invalidate the ballot paper.“Voters must write ‘1’ in the preference column next to the candidate of their choice.The figure ‘1’ must appear against only one candidate. Voters can then mark further preferences as 2, 3, or 4 against other contestants in order of choice,” election authorities said. Preferences must be indicated in figures only—such as 1, 2, 3; I, II, III; or १, २, ३ (in Devanagari script)—and not written in words.“Do not put tick marks or crosses, and do not write your name, initials, signature, or leave a thumb impression. A ballot where ‘1’ is not marked, or where ‘1’ is marked against more than one candidate, will be rejected,” said divisional commissioner of Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar and returning officer, G Sreekanth.Sreekanth also reviewed the election preparedness across Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Jalna, Beed, Latur, Dharashiv, Parbhani, Nanded, and Hingoli districts. The review covered basic amenities at polling stations, voter facilitation, availability of polling material, staff deployment, and security arrangements, alongside planning for party booths outside polling centres and safe transportation of ballot boxes.
Article Summary: 3,26,701 graduate voters will decide the fate of 41 candidates across 842 polling centres in eight districts. Political equations have turned messy across both Mahayuti and Maha Vikas Aghadi (MVA) camps. Two factions of Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) are largely battling this election as a fight for legacy.

Article Title: 63% graduates, 86% teachers turned out for Pune div MLC polls
Article Text:
Teachers after casting their votes for MLC election at Kolhapur's Main Rajaram School booth

Kolhapur:

BJP candidate accused of violating MCC

TOI





The estimated voter turnout in the Pune division MLC polls on Friday stood at 62.8% for the graduates’ constituency and 85.9% for the teachers’ constituency.Voting for the graduates’ constituency was held at 741 polling booths, while polling for the teachers’ constituency was conducted at 310 booths across Pune, Solapur, Sangli, Kolhapur and Satara districts.Of the 3,88,019 registered voters in the graduates’ constituency, as many as 2,43,611 cast their votes by the time polling closed at 4pm. In the teachers’ constituency, 53,185 of the 61,940 registered voters exercised their franchise.In the teachers’ constituency, Solapur led with 13,619 voters, followed by Pune (13,135), Kolhapur (10,899), Satara (8,451) and Sangli (7,081).In the graduates’ constituency, BJP ’s Smita Jadhav, an educationist and media owner, faced NCP (SP)’s Harshada Deshmukh Jadhav, an educationist and daughter of former IAS officer Prabhakar Deshmukh. Shiv Sena (UBT)’s Sunil Modi was also in the fray.The teachers’ constituency had a four-cornered contest involving BJP’s Kaustubh Gavade, sitting Congress MLC Jayant Asgaonkar and two independents — Shiv Sena-backed Sachin Sanap and Solapur’s Dattatray Sawant.Every six years, the MLC seats for the teachers’ and graduates’ constituencies get vacated and a fresh election is called. The voting takes place on ballot paper and the voters have to write numbers in the preference of their choice.While counting, if any one candidate gets past the winning quota of first-preference votes, he or she is declared a winner. If no clear winner emerges, the second-preference votes of each candidate are added to their first-preference votes, and so on and so forth, to get a clear winner. The counting is on Oct 27. The ballot boxes will be transferred to Balewadi in Pune for counting.BJP’s Pune MLC teachers’ constituency candidate Kaustubh Gavade cast his vote at a polling booth in Kolhapur. His video of going inside the booth and making a victory sign shows him wearing a stole with BJP's lotus symbols on it.Independent candidate Sachin Sanap, NCP (SP) MP Supriya Sule, MLA Rohit Pawar, Congress state president Harshwardhan Sapkal and several others took to their social media demanding action by Election Commission of India for violation of Model Code of Conduct.As per the MCC, a candidate or voter cannot bear anything related to a political party as it would be considered as campaigning on polling day, which is prohibited.tried to reach out to Gavade, but he was not available for comments.Meanwhile, independent candidate Dattatray Sawant alleged that voters were wooed by being given money by his rival candidates. He said that, per voter, Rs15,000 was distributed in the two to three days before the voting.Earlier, Congress MLC Satej Patil made similar claims and appealed to the Election Commission to take cognisance.
Article Summary: The estimated voter turnout in the Pune division MLC polls on Friday stood at 62.8% for the graduates’ constituency and 85.9% in the teachers' constituency. Of the 3,88,019 registered voters in the graduates' constituency, as many as 2,43,611 cast their votes by the time polling closed at 4pm. Solapur led with 13,619 voters, followed by Pune (13,135) and Kolhapur (10,899)

Article Title: Rs 1 lakh bribe trap: Navi Mumbai ACB catches circle officer, talathi and woman assistant
Article Text:
The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite, Jaihind Birsha Koli (49) and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36).





NAVI MUMBAI: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe from a villager in Chirner, Uran taluka, to register the names of his relatives in the 7/12 extract of a land record.The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36), an assistant to the revenue officials.Dharmaraj Sonake, deputy superintendent of police, Navi Mumbai ACB, said the complainant had applied to register the names of the heirs of his deceased sister in the 7/12 extract of their land in Chirner.The land was jointly owned by the complainant's maternal uncle, aunt, brother and sister. The complainant had also applied for deletion of his deceased brother's name and submitted the request to circle officer Mohite and talathi Koli. However, the two officials allegedly demanded Rs 1 lakh from him to process the work.Dy SP Sonake said, "After verification of the complaint on Monday, when it was confirmed that the revenue officers Mohite and Koli had told the complainant to hand over the bribe amount to the accused woman assistant Monika Patil, a trap was laid on Tuesday around 2 pm. After the woman assistant Monika Patil accepted the demanded bribe of Rs 1 lakh from the complainant and handed it over to circle officer Keshav Mohite, both were caught red-handed and arrested. While, the acccused Talathi Jaihind Koli who was involved in the bribe demand was taken into custody from Dronagiri."
Article Summary: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe. The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36)

Article Title: Man in Mahindra Thar with duplicate plate molests woman, knocks down another in Kharghar
Article Text:
30-year-old man was apprehended for allegedly molesting a woman and injuring another in Navi Mumbai.





NAVI MUMBAI: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team within 10 hours on Thursday evening.He had allegedly molested a 26-year-old woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night and, an hour later, severely injured a 22-year-old woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, Kharghar.Acting on a complaint by the woman allegedly molested by the Thar SUV driver, Kharghar police registered an FIR under BNS section 74 for the offence of assault or criminal force against a woman with the intent to outrage her modesty.While, as per the complaint by the injured woman Shrawani Dandekar, a resident of sector 3, Belpada, an FIR under relevant BNS sections and Motor Vehicle Act was registered against the Thar SUV driver for rash and negligent driving causing hurt.The detained aaccused identified as Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of sector 50, Seawoods, Nerul was handed over to Kharghar police for further legal action.Previously, in January 2021, he was arrested by Nerul police in the FIR registered against him for alleged kidnapping, sexual harassment and molestation of a woman.Sanjay Joshi, senior inspector of Kharghar said, "The accused Nakhvi has been detained and subsequently it will be decided whether to arrest him or serve with a notice under Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) for cooperating in police investigating."Audumbar Patil, senior inspector of crime branch unit-3 said, "After an FIR for molestation was registered at Kharghar police station by the victim woman, a resident of sector 34, Kharghar. As per the orders of higher authority, our team started a parallel probe. From the CCTV camera surveillance near the crime scene, we obtained the red Thar SUV's registration number, which was of Vashi RTO passing.""When verified, the registration number was found to be that of a Maruti WagonR car. As the accused had used a duplicate registration number plate, we scrutinized as many as 62 Thar SUVs registered with various Regional Transport Offices (RTOs). Subsequently, we obtained the registration number of a red Thar SUV that was registered with Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar RTO," Patil added.SPI Patil further informed, "The SUV was registered in the name of Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of Devaki Apartment in sector-50, Seawoods. From his mobile number registered with the RTO, his location was tracked.""He was apprehended from Bonkode village, Koparkhairane on Thursday late evening. Upon thorough interrogation, he confessed that he had inappropriately touched the woman pedestrian near Pethpada metro station while he drove his Thar SUV and sped away. He even confessed to have injured a woman pedestrian by hitting her his SUV while driving in Belpada area," he said.
Article Summary: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team on Thursday evening. He had allegedly molested a woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night. An hour later, he severely injured a woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, KharGHar.

Article Title: 2 women escape from RPF lockup in Navi Mumbai; 1 held after 6 hours, cop suspended
Article Text:
The women removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping. (AI image)





NAVI MUMBAI: In a major security lapse at Belapur Railway Protection Force (RPF), two women arrested for allegedly attempting to steal overhead electric wires from the Juinagar railway godown escaped from the lockup after midnight on September 28.One of them was apprehended around six hours later, while the other remains at large.The woman constable on night duty has been suspended and a departmental inquiry has been initiated against her.As per the FIR registered by RPF sub-inspector Milap Parte (52) at Panvel GRP, a case was registered on September 24 under Section 3(a) of the Railway Property (Unauthorized Possession) Act, 1966, Amendment 2012, at Belapur railway police station.The case was based on a written memo submitted by RPF personnel Ravikant Gade regarding the theft of overhead electric wires from the godown at Juinagar railway station on September 21.During the probe, a trap was laid on September 26 and around 1pm, two women were found loitering suspiciously near the Juinagar godown with the alleged intention of committing theft.They were taken into custody and identified as Rupali Kailas Kurhade (30), from Jalna, and Shalibai Ashok Pawar (49), from Bhiwandi.They were arrested after an FIR was registered for attempted theft and produced before a CSMT court, which remanded them to police custody till September 30. They were lodged in the lockup at Belapur RPF police station.Day-shift woman constable Rakhi Malaiya was assigned guard duty at the lockup, after which woman head constable Pooja Bagre was on night duty.Around 2am on September 28, when Bagre had gone to the toilet, the two women allegedly managed to open the lock by inserting their hands through the iron bars of the lockup and jerking it. Police suspect the lock may not have been secured properly.The women then reached the balcony at the rear end of the police station. They removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping.The incident was captured on CCTV footage. PSI Parte learnt about the escape after waking up at home around 6.30am and finding several missed calls from head constable Bagre and ASI Rajiv Parsan.Sunil Nila, chief spokesperson of Central Railway, said, "One accused woman Rupali Kurhade was apprehended from near Nerul railway station around 8.45 am. The other accused Shalibai Pawar is still absconding."
Article Summary: The women removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping. One of them was apprehended around six hours later, while the other remains at large. The woman constable on night duty has been suspended and a departmental inquiry has been initiated.

Article Title: TMC suspends fire chief over immersion ghats lapses
Article Text:
Thane municipal corporation





THANE: The Thane municipal corporation (TMC) on Friday suspended its acting chief fire officer (CFO) over alleged negligence in providing adequate safety equipment at idol immersion ghats on Oct 20. Action has also been taken against two other officials, while show-cause notices have been served on two junior staff, it is learnt.The suspension order is issued by additional municipal commissioner-1, Prashant Rode, holds Jhalke responsible for lapses in carrying out his duties. The order states that he has been suspended under the Maharashtra Civil Services (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1979. Jhalke, who is the fire officer and in-charge of Balkum fire station, has been handling the additional charge of CFO for the last several years."Certain safety arrangements at Datta Mandir Ghat and Ahilyadevi Ghat at Masunda Lake were allegedly found to be inadequate, with a particular shortfall in life jackets and other essential safety equipment. The shortcomings were apparently pointed out to deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde who also expressed concern at the alleged negligence," said a civic official.Officials said that during the suspension period, Jhalke will be required to comply with the prescribed conditions and cannot take up other employment or engage in business without the requisite permission.
Article Summary: Thane municipal corporation suspends acting chief fire officer (CFO) over alleged negligence. Action also taken against two other officials, while show- cause notices have been served on two junior staff. Safety arrangements at Datta Mandir Ghat and Ahilyadevi Ghat at Masunda Lake allegedly found to be inadequate.

Article Title: Sealed Thane flat in Iqbal Kaskar-Dawood Ibrahim money laundering case breached; ED reclaims property, files FIR
Article Text:
Thane flat linked to Iqbal Kaskar’s extortion case targeted for occupation





MUMBAI: Enforcement Directorate (ED) filed an FIR for trespassing and attempting to occupy a flat in Thane which was attached in a money laundering case it investigated against Iqbal Kaskar and his Pakistan-based gangster brother Dawood Ibrahim The flat was attached in the case in 2022, in the money laundering case linked to extortion by Iqbal Kaskar and others.The flat was in ED’s possession and it had put its seal on the lock. Kaskar had acquired the flat through extortion and threat in 2015 and got it registered in the name of his associate Mumtaz Azaz Sheikh, alias Raju.Recently, the ED learnt that certain persons entered the flat after removing its possession notice, claiming ownership of the flat.Since the money laundering case is pending in the court, the ED informed the court about it, repossessed the flat and filed a police case last week.
Article Summary: Enforcement Directorate (ED) filed an FIR for trespassing and attempting to occupy a flat in Thane. The flat was attached in a money laundering case it investigated against Iqbal Kaskar and his Pakistan-based gangster brother Dawood Ibrahim. The ED repossessed the flat and filed a police case last week.

Article Title: Ulhasnagar social activist Haresh Gajwani shot dead outside railway station, 3 arrested
Article Text:
Haresh Gajwani was murdered outside Ulhasnagar railway station on Wednesday night.





ULHASNAGAR: Police have arrested three suspects in connection with the murder of social worker Haresh Gajwani, who was shot dead outside Ulhasnagar railway station on Wednesday night. The suspects have been identified as Avinash Naidu, Vijay Singh and Noor Alam Khan.According to preliminary investigations, Gajwani and Naidu had a long-standing dispute. In 2021, counter-cases were registered against the two sides following a dispute, which allegedly contributed to continuing tensions between Gajwani and the accused.Police said the three suspects were traced and detained with the help of CCTV footage. Investigators are examining the alleged past rivalry, along with other possible motives behind the murder.Gajwani, 54, was allegedly attacked by three assailants who fired two rounds at him before fleeing the scene. Locals and police took him to Central Hospital, where doctors declared him "brought dead".Recently, Gajwani had posted on X, tagging senior officials from various police departments, as well as the chief minister, deputy chief minister and FDA commissioner Tukaram Mundhe. In his posts, he had highlighted alleged illegal activities in the area and claimed that some police personnel were supporting those involved. He had also expressed fears for his life, warning that the police personnel he had accused would also be responsible if anything happened to him.
Article Summary: Haresh Gajwani, 54, was shot dead outside Ulhasnagar railway station on Wednesday. Police have arrested three suspects in connection with the murder. The suspects have been identified as Avinash Naidu, Vijay Singh and Noor Alam Khan. Investigators are examining the alleged past rivalry, along with other possible motives.

Article Title: Cong MLA Wadettiwar Says Mahayuti Govt Unmasked By Audio Clip
Article Text:
Nagpur:





Congress MLA Vijay Wadettiwar on Friday accused CM Devendra Fadnavis and Deputy CM Eknath Shinde of pitting Marathas against OBCs to grab power and demanded an inquiry into the Rs 500-crore funding mentioned in an audio clip released by quota activist Manoj Jarange.Wadettiwar said, “I congratulate Jarange for bringing out this audio. The govt is unmasked before the people. It also shows how BJP and Shinde-Sena are hungry for power,” he said.Attacking Mahayuti parties over the Maratha-OBC rift, he said, “Eknath bhai and Devabhau pitted Marathas against OBCs and ruined the state by fuelling unrest. Once in power, they are now locked in a tussle for the chair,” he said.Demanding a probe into the audio clip, Wadettiwar said, “Calling the clip fabricated is wrong and nobody will accept it. But one thing is clear, the rift between Mahayuti partners has reached its worst phase. It also shows how money was spent to trigger unrest and quell agitations,” he said.On whether the probe should be by ED, he said the agency did not matter. “Do it through ED or CBI, but bring the facts on the table. If someone is being defamed, truth must come out,” he said.He added the audio clip controversy was a huge distraction. “There is a drought, the jobless are on the roads, exam papers are being leaked and MPSC is in a mess, but they don’t care,” he said.
Article Summary: Congress MLA Vijay Wadettiwar accused CM Devendra Fadnavis and Deputy CM Eknath Shinde of pitting Marathas against OBCs. He demanded an inquiry into the Rs 500-crore funding mentioned in an audio clip released by quota activist Manoj Jarange.

Article Title: Fadnavis Orders Forensic Probe Into Audio Clip Released By Jarange
Article Text:
Nagpur:





Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis on Friday said the audio clip released by Maratha quota spearhead, Manoj Jarange, would undergo a forensic investigation and the truth would be brought out.The audio clip is of a conversation that alleges BJP paid Rs 500 crore to Jarange through Deputy CM Eknath Shinde ’s son, Shrikant Shinde, a Lok Sabha MP, to silence the activist and weaken the Maratha reservation agitation, which started over three years ago.Speaking after voting in the Nagpur division graduates’ constituency election, Fadnavis said a Shiv Sena delegation met him on the issue. “Now, whatever conversation has come out, will be investigated fully and forensically. I have given the same assurance to the Sena delegation,” said the CM.Fadnavis, however, questioned the timing of the audio clip’s release. “All of us are asking why this audio conversation is coming out after two-and-half years. What’s the motive and who is being targeted and why? There are many such questions,” he said.Responding to NCP (SP) MP Supriya Sule ’s allegations of misconduct by BJP in MLC polls, Fadnavis said the former must provide more information. Sule had alleged BJP was using pens equipped with spy cams for distributing money.Fadnavis sarcastically said “What exactly is a spy pen and how does it work? If Sule sends it to me, I will understand more about the pen and find out what is going on.”
Article Summary: The audio clip is of a conversation that alleges BJP paid Rs 500 crore to Jarange through Deputy CM Eknath Shinde ’s son. Fadnavis, however, questioned the timing of the audio clip’s release. “All of us are asking why this audio conversation is coming out after two-and-half years,” he said.

Article Title: 4 drunk men told to deboard MSRTC bus smash windshield
Article Text:
Nagpur:





Four men allegedly damaged the rear windshield of a Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation (MSRTC) bus by hurling stones near the Mankapur Ring Road signal late Thursday night.The incident occurred around 10pm when the bus operating from the Koradi depot was travelling from Sitabuldi to Parseoni Fata. As per sources, the four men were intoxicated while travelling in the bus and caused inconvenience to fellow passengers while watching videos on their mobile phones at a high volume.When some passengers objected, the four men reportedly got off the bus, picked up stones from the roadside and threw them at the bus. They then fled from the spot near the Mankapur Ring Road signal.The bus was being driven by Nikhil Shende, while Vaibhav Dhawale was on conductor duty.The incident was reported to Mankapur police station. Police are examining CCTV footage of the bus to identify those responsible.
Article Summary: Four men allegedly damaged the rear windshield of a Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation (MSRTC) bus by hurling stones. The incident occurred around 10pm when the bus operating from the Koradi depot was travelling from Sitabuldi to Parseoni Fata. Police are examining CCTV footage of the bus to identify those responsible.

Article Title: TVK, DMK walk out of Chennai electoral roll meeting
Article Text:
Tamil Nadu chief minister and TVK party chief C Joseph Vijay

Chennai:





Nine of the 13 recognised parties in Tamil Nadu, including TVK and DMK , walked out of ECI’s all-party meeting on special summary revision (SSR) of electoral rolls, protesting alleged irregularities in special intensive revision (SIR) exercise. While AIADMK and BJP participated, leaders of BSP did not turn up for the meeting chaired by chief electoral officer Archana Patnaik at the secretariat on Friday.Electricity minister C T R Nirmalkumar said TVK was always opposed to SIR. “We had asked the ECI to rectify the irregularities during SIR exercise to ensure free and fair elections. Without addressing that issue, special summary revision should not be taken up,” Nirmalkumar told reporters after walking out of the meeting. He further said that the chief election commissioner (CEC) should resign for the alleged irregularities in SIR.DMK deputy organisational secretary S Austin along with legal wing joint secretary I Paranthamen registered their views on SIR in the meeting and walked out. “We demanded an explanation from ECI on the steps that would be taken to enrol the 74 lakh voters who were removed from the electoral rolls during the SIR in Tamil Nadu.We also asked when the re- enrolment process would begin. But there was no response from the authorities,” Paranthamen said.Noting that DMK has been demanding the removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar over SIR, he said DMK would continue its protest against SIR. Paranthamen said DMK was also planning to meet the President to submit a memorandum on the issue.Representatives of CPI, CPM, VCK, DMDK, AAP and Congress also walked out of the meeting, demanding the rollback of SIR and resignation of Gyanesh Kumar.Describing the political parties’ walkout as their “democratic right”, former AIADMK minister D Jayakumar said but equated their response to the criticism of EVMs when parties get defeated. He, however, said the AIADMK was not defending any individual, including Gyanesh Kumar, but was insisting that the ECI take appropriate measures to include the 52 lakh voters removed on the grounds of having shifted residence, four lakh removed due to duplicate entries, and 13 lakh categorised as permanently shifted.Representatives from National People’s Party attended the meeting.
Article Summary: Nine of the 13 recognised parties in Tamil Nadu, including TVK and DMK, walked out of ECI’s all-party meeting on special summary revision (SSR) of electoral rolls. While AIADMK and BJP participated, leaders of BSP did not turn up.

Article Title: HC grants bail to man who created AI videos of CM to scam people
Article Text: Chennai: Madras high court on Friday granted conditional bail to a Rajasthani man who allegedly created fake AI videos of Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay and scammed people. The court has directed him to appear before the investigating officer daily.Justice N Ramesh passed the order on an application moved by Shyabu Khan, a resident of Alwar district, Rajasthan . The court granted the relief since Shyabu Khan was in jail since Sept 12 and the police have completed the investigation.Shyabu Khan was charged for offences under Sections 204, 318(2) (cheating), 319(2) (cheating by personation), 336(3) (forgery), and 340(2) (use of forged document) of the BNS, and Sections 66C (identity theft) and 66D of the Information Technology Act.According to the prosecution, he had generated AI videos on social media impersonating chief minister C Joseph Vijay with the intention of inducing the public. It was submitted that the man had created two social media profiles and circulated AI videos asking the general public to contact them for any help and collected registration fee from public.On Friday, when the plea came up for hearing, the petitioner submitted that he was innocent and that one of his friends had created fake social media accounts and used his bank account to commit the offence.
Article Summary: Rajasthani man allegedly created fake AI videos of Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay and scammed people. It was submitted that the man had created two social media profiles and circulated AI videos asking the general public to contact them.

Article Title: Youth hacks woman to death, abducts daughters
Article Text:

The accused then abducted the girl with whom he was in love as well as her 14-year-old sibling, a class VIII student, on his two-wheeler.On receiving information, police rushed to the spot, shifted the injured to hospital and sent Mary Vijila’s body to Tirunelveli Govt Medical College Hospital for postmortem. Article Title: Madras HC orders release of Thanjavur DCB inspector, says his arrest, remand are illegal
Article Text:
Madurai:





Cleared/375 WordsHolding that the arrest and remand of suspended Thanjavur DCB inspector Sugumaran in connection with an extortion case were illegal as the grounds of arrest were not served to him, Madras high court on Friday ordered that he should be released forthwith.The court was hearing the habeas corpus petition filed by Innisai, wife of Sugumaran. The CB-CID arrested Sugumaran for allegedly extorting Rs5 crore in a dispute between the partners of a private hospital in the district.A division bench of Justice G R Swaminathan and Justice P Murugan observed, “We wanted the authorities to satisfy us that proper reasons were recorded for justifying the arrest of Sugumaran when he had duly complied with the notice issued under Section 35(3) of BNSS, 2023. We place on record that no material was placed before us to show that the requirement set out in Section 35(5) was complied with. This alone is more than sufficient to declare the arrest and remand of Sugumaran as illegal. ”Expressing shock and surprise, the judges said, “The prosecution did not claim that the grounds of arrest had been served. No such finding was recorded by the trial magistrate. On the other hand, according to the trial magistrate, the fact that the arrestee is a police officer and that his spouse is a lawyer are circumstances that justify dispensing with the constitutional requirement.We remind the officer that Article 21 and 22 are sacrosanct. Certain fundamental rights are non-negotiable. Even the doctrine of waiver would not apply.”The judges observed that they are not concerned with the merits of the matter. “We, therefore, will not be justified in holding that the FIR registered by CB-CID has to be quashed. That is an independent battle which Sugumaran may have to wage. Whether the fundamental rights of Sugumaran were breached in the matter of his arrest and remand is the only point for consideration before us. No doubt, Sugumaran is a police officer accused of having played ‘Katta panchayat’. But even such a person deserves due process.”Hence, the judges declared that the petitioner’s husband’s arrest, detention and subsequent remand are illegal. He shall be released forthwith. “We are not granting bail. We are directing his unconditional release,” the judges observed.
Article Summary: The court was hearing the habeas corpus petition filed by Innisai, wife of Sugumaran. He was arrested for allegedly extorting Rs5 crore in a dispute between the partners of a private hospital in the district. The judges observed that they are not concerned with the merits of the matter.

Article Title: HC strikes down Keralam govt guidelines restricting production of arrested persons before magistrates, doctors after 5pm
Article Text:
Kochi

:





The high court has struck down key clauses in the guidelines for producing accused persons before registered medical practitioners and judicial officers, which required arrested persons to be produced before judicial officers “as far as possible” between 10am and 5pm and permitted production after 5pm only in “exceptional circumstances”.A bench of Justices V Raja Vijayaraghavan and K V Jayakumar issued the order on a PIL filed by P S Subeesh, a lawyer from Irinjalakuda in Thrissur, challenging the clauses in the guidelines governing the production of accused persons before registered medical practitioners in hospitals or judicial officers for medical examination and medico-legal procedures. The state govt had issued the guidelines in the aftermath of the death of Dr Vandana Das, a house surgeon at Taluk Hospital, Kottarakkara, who was attacked by an accused brought to the hospital by police for a medical examination in 2023.The petitioner challenged Clauses 17 to 21 of the guidelines, which imposed reporting, attendance and monitoring requirements on police and prosecutors for production outside regular hours. He further argued that the expressions ‘as far as possible’ and ‘exceptional circumstances’ could undermine the constitutional mandate for production before a magistrate within 24 hours of arrest and compel police officers and prosecutors to justify compliance with the prescribed protocol.The state defended the guidelines, saying they were framed after Dr Vandana Das’s death and did not dilute the 24-hour limit under Article 22(2) of the Constitution and Section 58 of the BNSS.The court held that the 24-hour period is an outer limit, not a licence to defer production until the deadline approaches. It observed that the expressions “as far as possible” and “exceptional circumstances” could create a practical disincentive to prompt production, delaying judicial scrutiny, access to legal aid and the accused’s opportunity to challenge the arrest or seek bail. An executive protocol, the bench said, cannot dilute constitutional and statutory safeguards or subordinate them to administrative convenience. The court directed the state to issue fresh guidelines in accordance with its findings.
Article Summary: Justices V Raja Vijayaraghavan and K V Jayakumar issued the order on a PIL filed by P S Subeesh, a lawyer from Irinjalakuda in Thrissur. The court held that the 24-hour period is an outer limit, not a licence to defer production until the deadline approaches.
